audit.title: Automation Contracts

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Strong; each section opens with the contract and a self-contained purpose, e.g. "The registry contract that tracks all registered Upkeeps and the Automation Nodes that can perform them." No cross-reference dependencies.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Good — 6 clean sections, 0 level skips, all under 98 words. Weak spot: the `AutomationCompatible.sol` inventory sits as a bullet list under the H1 with no H2, and there is no summary table for at-a-glance extraction.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Thin — 5 numerals, 0 with units, no deployed addresses or supported networks. Version strings (`v1.3.0`, `2.1`, `1.2/1.3/2.0`) are the main specifics; a reference page like this should name registry addresses or at least link the network address table.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong; 9 primary-source GitHub links pinned to a release tag. One opaque `here` link weakens attribution.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good — the Forwarder description ("a relayer that sits between the registry and the customer's target contract") is crisply liftable. Most contracts get a one-sentence definition near first mention.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no datePublished/dateModified. Head metadata was not captured, so absence of `og`/`TechArticle` schema can't be fully verified, but nothing in the served HTML supplies freshness or entity signals.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: Weak — 0 code fences. Acceptable for a pure link index, but a minimal import example (`import "@chainlink/contracts/src/v0.8/automation/AutomationCompatible.sol";`) would make it agent-runnable.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Adequate for "what contracts does Chainlink Automation use," but no symptom/how-to entry points and no FAQ.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Mostly clear; the `AutomationRegistry.sol` heading naming a `2_1` contract, and the `AutomationRegistrar.sol` heading likewise, introduce name inconsistency that hurts entity resolution.

audit.summary: This is a compact reference page cataloging the core Chainlink Automation contracts, and its main GEO strength is dense, authoritative sourcing — 9 of 14 links point directly to canonical GitHub source (`contracts-v1.3.0`). Its biggest opportunities are structural and metadata: the contract inventory belongs in a summary table (currently 0 tables), and the page carries no JSON-LD, canonical URL, or last-updated signal. A visible entity mismatch (heading `AutomationRegistry.sol` vs. body `AutomationRegistry2_1.sol`) risks confusing entity resolution. Solid but under-optimized for lift-and-cite.

recommendations.title: Add a summary contract table
recommendations.where: top of page, after the intro paragraph
recommendations.issue: contracts are listed as scattered H2s with prose; 0 tables.
recommendations.change: add a table with columns `Contract | Source file (version) | Purpose | When to use`, one row per contract, each linking the pinned GitHub source.
recommendations.why: tables are high-lift for extraction and let engines build a justified "which contract do I need" answer in one chunk.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` + canonical URL + dateModified
recommendations.change: emit `TechArticle` schema with `headline`, `dateModified`, and a self-referential `canonical`.
recommendations.why: freshness and canonical signals raise E-E-A-T and parse trust for agents; their absence is a measured deficit.

recommendations.title: Fix heading/contract entity mismatch
recommendations.change: align headings to the versioned artifact, e.g. `## AutomationRegistry (v2.1)` and note the abstract role in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: consistent naming prevents engines conflating or mis-attributing the contract entity.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/how-to phrased sub-headings or intro line
recommendations.issue: no headings match "which contract do I import for Automation" / "what is the Automation registry address".
recommendations.change: add a one-line answer-first lead: "To make a contract Automation-compatible, import `AutomationCompatible.sol`; the on-chain registry is `AutomationRegistry`, and registration goes through `AutomationRegistrar`." Optionally add a "Which contract do I need?" line.
recommendations.why: captures intent-phrased retrieval that a bare contract catalog misses.

recommendations.title: Replace opaque link text
recommendations.change: relabel to "the Register Upkeeps programmatically guide".
recommendations.why: descriptive anchors improve link context for both engines and agents.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal import snippet
recommendations.issue: 0 fenced code blocks; agents can't copy an import.
recommendations.why: gives agents a runnable, copy-pasteable artifact tied to the exact package path.

antiPatterns: Opaque anchor text (`here`) in the CronUpkeepFactory section.
Undated content — no visible last-updated signal.
Minor entity inconsistency between section headings and the contracts they describe.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; confirm this reference page is enumerated there.
Site-level `TechArticle`/breadcrumb schema and a freshness cadence are best set globally rather than per-page.
The CLI should pass raw `<head>` so canonical/OG/schema presence can be fully verified rather than inferred from served HTML.
